q: Any increase in pressure at the surface of an enclosed fluid must be transmitted to ____ in the fluid.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. Any increase in pressure at the surface of an enclosed fluid must be transmitted to every other point in the fluid.

q: This concept was first recognized by French scientist ____ in 1650.
e: This concept was first recognized by French scientist Balise Pascal in 1650. Balise pascal is what this statement is using.

q: When a fluid completely fills a vessel and a pressure is applied to it at any part of the surface, that pressure is transmitted ____ throughout the whole of the enclosed fluid.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. When a fluid completely fills a vessel and a pressure is applied to it at any part of the surface, that pressure is transmitted equally throughout the whole of the enclosed fluid.
This is known as Pascal's law. The name used here is Pascal's law.

q: The concept of Pascal's law is very useful in practice in the working principle of the ____ and hydraulic presses.
e: Pressure is force over area. The SI unit is the pascal, N m⁻². The concept of Pascal's law is very useful in practice in the working principle of the hydraulic brakes and hydraulic presses.

q: A hydraulic press is used for baling jute, hay, cotton and also for the pressing of the ____ and for shaping steel and metal sheets.
e: A hydraulic press is used for baling jute, hay, cotton and also for the pressing of the automobile bodies and for shaping steel and metal sheets. Automobile bodies is what this statement is using.
Therefore it is named force multiplier. Force multiplier is what this statement is using.

q: According to Pascal's law, the pressure $p_{in}$ is equal to the pressure ____ exerted on area $A_{out}$ of large piston.
e: Pressure is force over area. The SI unit is the pascal, N m⁻². According to Pascal's law, the pressure pin is equal to the pressure pout exerted on area Aout of large piston.

q: The upward force $F_{out}$ on area $A_{out}$ is $F_{out} =$ ____.
e: The upward force Fout on area Aout is Fout = pin × Aout. Leave the relation as pin × Aout.

q: Assuming there is no friction in the hydraulic press system, the work done by effort equals the ____ done by the upward force.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. Assuming there is no friction in the hydraulic press system, the work done by effort equals the work done by the upward force.

q: where $l_{in}$ = the distance travelled by ____ piston.
e: Where lin = the distance travelled by small piston. Small is what this statement is using.
Lout = the distance travelled by large piston. Large is what this statement is using.

q: Another useful machine based on Pascal's law is a ____ lift.
e: Pressure is force over area. The SI unit is the pascal, N m⁻². Another useful machine based on Pascal's law is a hydraulic lift.

q: By applying a small force on the small piston produces a large upward force on the large piston which can lift a large ____.
e: By applying a small force on the small piston produces a large upward force on the large piston which can lift a large load. Load is what this statement is using.
